chosen_property.label: banTarget
chosen_property.definition: A relation between a prohibition event and the product or organization that is prohibited.

candidates.label: travelBans
candidates.comment: A travel bans relation between a special announcement and information regarding restrictions on travel. Also called travel restrictions, ban on travel, travel advisories. Examples: "SpecialAnnouncement travelBans 'https://example.com/travel-restrictions'", "SpecialAnnouncement travelBans 'All international travel is suspended.'", "SpecialAnnouncement travelBans 'https://who.int/travel-guidance'".

candidates.label: permittedUsage
candidates.comment: A descriptive attribute indicating the allowed uses or activities within an accommodation. Also called allowed uses, usage rules, permitted activities. Examples: An apartment has a permitted usage of 'Residential Only'. A hotel room has a permitted usage of 'Short-term Stay'. A conference hall has a permitted usage of 'Events and Meetings'.

candidates.label: countryOfLastProcessing
candidates.comment: A final processing location relation between a product and the country where it underwent its last processing and testing before importation. Also called: last processed in, final testing country, pre-importation processing location. Examples: "Electronic Component" country of last processing "Malaysia", "Textile Product" country of last processing "Bangladesh", "Automotive Part" country of last processing "Thailand". Distinct from countryOfOrigin, which is about the origin of the product itself.

candidates.label: legislationJurisdiction
candidates.comment: A jurisdiction relation between a piece of legislation and the administrative area from which it originates. Also called: originating jurisdiction, legal territory, governing region. Examples: "Federal Law legislationJurisdiction United States", "State Statute legislationJurisdiction California", "EU Directive legislationJurisdiction European Union".

candidates.label: countriesNotSupported
candidates.comment: A geographical restriction relation between a software application and the countries where it is not supported. Also called: unsupported regions, restricted countries, unavailable in. Examples: "App X" countries not supported "Cuba", "Software Y" countries not supported "Iran, North Korea", "Game Z" countries not supported "Syria". Distinct from countriesSupported, which lists where the application is supported.

candidates.label: legislationPassedBy
candidates.comment: A passing authority relation between a piece of legislation and the organization or person that originally enacted it. Also called: enacted by, made by, legislated by. Examples: "Primary Legislation legislationPassedBy Parliament", "Secondary Legislation legislationPassedBy Government", "Local Bylaw legislationPassedBy City Council". Distinct from legislationResponsible, which refers to the ministry or individual in charge of elaborating or addressing questions about the legislation.

candidates.label: regionsAllowed
candidates.comment: A regions allowed relation between a media object and the geographical areas where its use is permitted. Also called allowed in, permitted regions, geographical availability. Examples: "A movie streaming service has regions allowed 'US, Canada'.", "A music video has regions allowed 'Europe'.", "A software download has regions allowed 'Worldwide'."

candidates.label: isConsumableFor
candidates.comment: A product dependency relation between a product and the other products that consume it or require it for operation. Also called consumable for, used by, required by, compatible consumable. Examples: An ink cartridge isConsumableFor 'Printer Model X'. Coffee pods areConsumableFor 'Coffee Machine Y'. Batteries areConsumableFor 'Remote Control Z'. Distinct from isAccessoryOrSparePartFor, which refers to items that are not used up.

candidates.label: seller
candidates.comment: The organization or person that offers, sells, leases, lends, or loans goods or services. Also called vendor, merchant, provider, retailer. Examples: `BuyAction` seller `Amazon`, `Offer for Product` seller `Best Buy`, `Flight Booking` seller `Airline X`. Distinct from `customer` or `buyer`.

candidates.label: manufacturer
candidates.comment: A manufacturing relation between a product and the organization that produced it. Also called: produced by, made by, fabricated by. Examples: "Smartphone manufacturer Apple", "Automobile manufacturer Toyota", "Furniture manufacturer IKEA".

chosen_property.label: governmentAction
chosen_property.definition: A relation between a country and a government-related event or statement.

candidates.label: governmentBenefitsInfo
candidates.comment: A government benefits info relation between a special announcement and information about associated government services or benefits. Also called: public aid details, government assistance, benefit programs. Examples: "Pandemic Relief Announcement" government benefits info "Unemployment Benefits Program", "Housing Crisis Alert" government benefits info "Rental Assistance Program", "Disaster Recovery Notice" government benefits info "FEMA Aid Services".

candidates.label: serviceOperator
candidates.comment: The organization responsible for operating a government service, distinct from the primary provider. Also called service management, operating entity, service subcontractor. Examples: `Public Transport Service` serviceOperator `Transit Authority`, `Waste Collection Service` serviceOperator `Private Waste Management Company`, `National Park Service` serviceOperator `Local Park Management`. Distinct from `provider`, which is the primary organization offering the service.

candidates.label: legislationPassedBy
candidates.comment: A passing authority relation between a piece of legislation and the organization or person that originally enacted it. Also called: enacted by, made by, legislated by. Examples: "Primary Legislation legislationPassedBy Parliament", "Secondary Legislation legislationPassedBy Government", "Local Bylaw legislationPassedBy City Council". Distinct from legislationResponsible, which refers to the ministry or individual in charge of elaborating or addressing questions about the legislation.

candidates.label: legislationJurisdiction
candidates.comment: A jurisdiction relation between a piece of legislation and the administrative area from which it originates. Also called: originating jurisdiction, legal territory, governing region. Examples: "Federal Law legislationJurisdiction United States", "State Statute legislationJurisdiction California", "EU Directive legislationJurisdiction European Union".

candidates.label: legislationLegalValue
candidates.comment: A legal value relation between a legislation file and its level of legal authority. Also called: legal authority, official value, legal weight. Examples: "Digitally Signed PDF legislationLegalValue StrongerLegalValue", "HTML Version legislationLegalValue WeakerLegalValue", "Certified Copy legislationLegalValue HighLegalValue".

candidates.label: legislationIdentifier
candidates.comment: An identifier relation between a piece of legislation and its unique string or URL-based identifier. Also called: legal identifier, official ID, legislative code. Examples: "EU Regulation 2016/679 legislationIdentifier CELEX:32016R0679", "French Law legislationIdentifier NOR:XXXXXX", "UK Act legislationIdentifier URN-Lex:XXXX".

candidates.label: legislationAmends
candidates.comment: A legislative modification relation between a piece of legislation and another legislation that it alters or revises. Also called amends law, modifies legislation, revises act, changes statute. Examples: Legislation A legislationAmends 'Legislation B'. The new act legislationAmends 'the previous statute'. This bill legislationAmends 'the tax code'. Distinct from legislationChanges, which is a broader term for any change, whereas legislationAmends specifically introduces legal changes.

candidates.label: legislationEnsuresImplementationOf
candidates.comment: An implementation assurance relation between two pieces of legislation, where one ensures the implementation of the other by modifying national laws. Also called: implements, ensures compliance with, enforces. Examples: "National Law A legislationEnsuresImplementationOf EU Regulation B", "State Statute legislationEnsuresImplementationOf Federal Act", "Local Ordinance legislationEnsuresImplementationOf Regional Directive". Distinct from legislationTransposes, which specifically refers to fulfilling objectives by passing implementation measures.

candidates.label: legislationCountersignedBy
candidates.comment: A countersignature relation between a piece of legislation and the person or organization that countersigned it. Also called: countersigned by, officially endorsed by, co-signed by. Examples: "The Bill of Rights legislationCountersignedBy President Washington", "EU Directive 2023/45 legislationCountersignedBy European Commission", "Local Ordinance legislationCountersignedBy City Clerk".

candidates.label: taxID
candidates.comment: An identification of the tax or fiscal ID for an organization or person. Also called "fiscal ID", "tax identification number", "TIN", "VAT number". Examples: "The organization has taxID 12-3456789", "The person's taxID is their Social Security Number", "This company's taxID is its CIF."

chosen_property.label: targetCountry
chosen_property.definition: A relation indicating that an event is targeted at a specific country.

candidates.label: target
candidates.comment: A destination relation between an action and its intended entry point or URL. Also called "action destination", "target URL", "entry point for action", "leads to". Examples: "The search action has target a search results page", "The button's target is a specific URL", "This action points to a target entry point."

candidates.label: targetName
candidates.comment: A textual name of a node within an established educational framework. Also called "framework node name", "educational standard name", "learning objective name". Examples: "The alignment object has targetName 'Algebra I'", "The educational framework node's targetName is 'Critical Thinking'", "This targetName identifies a specific skill."

candidates.label: targetUrl
candidates.comment: A URL identifying a node within an established educational framework. Also called "framework node URL", "educational standard URL", "learning objective URL". Examples: "The alignment object has targetUrl 'http://example.com/algebra-standard'", "The educational framework node's targetUrl points to its definition", "This targetUrl links to a specific competency."

candidates.label: targetProduct
candidates.comment: A compatibility relation between software source code and the software application or operating system it is intended for. Also called "compatible with", "designed for", "applies to product", "software target". Examples: "The source code has targetProduct Windows 10", "The script's targetProduct is Microsoft Excel", "This code is written for targetProduct Linux."

candidates.label: targetDescription
candidates.comment: A textual description of a node within an established educational framework. Also called "framework node description", "educational standard description", "learning objective description". Examples: "The alignment object has targetDescription 'Understand basic algebra'", "The educational framework node's targetDescription explains the competency", "This targetDescription details a specific learning outcome."

candidates.label: targetPlatform
candidates.comment: An identification of the type of platform for which an API reference is intended, such as phone or desktop. Also called "platform type", "development platform", "operating system target", "device target". Examples: "The API reference has targetPlatform iOS", "The software's targetPlatform is Windows Desktop", "This API is designed for targetPlatform Android."

candidates.label: targetCollection
candidates.comment: A specific collection relation between an update action and the collection of things that is the target of the action. Also called "collection to update", "target set", "destination collection". Examples: "The add action has targetCollection a list of items", "The update action's targetCollection is a database table", "This action modifies a targetCollection of documents.". Distinct from object, which is a more general target of an action.

candidates.label: object
candidates.comment: A thing upon which an action is carried out, potentially changing its state. Also called target, item acted upon, recipient of action. Examples: "Read Action object 'a book'", "Buy Action object 'a product'", "Edit Action object 'a document'". Distinct from instrument, which is the tool used to perform the action.

candidates.label: targetPopulation
candidates.comment: A textual description of the characteristics of the intended or typical population for a dietary supplement or dose schedule. Also called "intended users", "demographic target", "user group", "audience characteristics". Examples: "The supplement has targetPopulation 'adults'", "The dose schedule's targetPopulation is 'children aged 6-12'", "This product is designed for a targetPopulation of athletes."

candidates.label: permitAudience
candidates.comment: A targeting relation between a permit and the specific audience it is intended for. Also called target group, eligible recipients, intended users. Examples: A fishing permit has a permit audience of 'Local Residents'. A building permit has a permit audience of 'Licensed Contractors'. A student permit has a permit audience of 'University Students'.

candidates.label: inSupportOf
candidates.comment: A support relation between a thesis and the qualification, candidature, degree, or application it supports. Also called supports for, for the purpose of, in aid of. Examples: "A thesis is in support of a PhD degree.", "The research is in support of a qualification.", "This thesis is written in support of an application."

candidates.label: sponsor
candidates.comment: A support relation between an entity (creative work, event, grant, study, organization, or person) and the person or organization providing financial or other backing. Also called "funded by", "supported by", "patron", "underwritten by". Examples: "The event has sponsor Acme Corp", "The medical study's sponsor is the NIH", "This artist has sponsor a private foundation."

candidates.label: recommendationStrength
candidates.comment: A recommendation strength relation between a medical guideline recommendation and its categorized level of evidence or support. Also called strength of evidence, guideline strength. Examples: "A medical guideline recommendation has a recommendation strength 'Class I'.", "A treatment guideline has a recommendation strength 'Strong'.", "A diagnostic recommendation has a recommendation strength 'Grade B'."

candidates.label: supportingData
candidates.comment: A data relation between a software application and the data feed that provides supplementary information or content. Also called "supplementary data", "data feed for", "application data source". Examples: "The mapping application has supportingData a traffic data feed", "The software application's supportingData is a weather feed", "This program uses supportingData for real-time updates."

candidates.label: study
candidates.comment: A relation between a medical entity and a medical study or trial that investigates it. Also called "related study", "investigated by study", "medical trial". Examples: "The drug has study a clinical trial", "The medical condition is part of a study", "This therapy is being evaluated in a study."

candidates.label: valueRequired
candidates.comment: A value required relation between a property value specification and whether the property must be filled to complete an action. Also called mandatory field, required property, input necessity. Examples: "PropertyValueSpecification valueRequired 'true'", "PropertyValueSpecification valueRequired 'false'", "Form field valueRequired 'true'".

candidates.label: legislationPassedBy
candidates.comment: A passing authority relation between a piece of legislation and the organization or person that originally enacted it. Also called: enacted by, made by, legislated by. Examples: "Primary Legislation legislationPassedBy Parliament", "Secondary Legislation legislationPassedBy Government", "Local Bylaw legislationPassedBy City Council". Distinct from legislationResponsible, which refers to the ministry or individual in charge of elaborating or addressing questions about the legislation.

candidates.label: isBasedOn
candidates.comment: A derivation relation between a creative work and the resource (another work, product, or URL) from which it is adapted or modified. Also called derived from, adapted from, based on, inspired by, modification of. Examples: A movie isBasedOn 'a novel'. A software update isBasedOn 'previous version'. A remix isBasedOn 'original song'. Distinct from isBasedOnUrl, which specifically points to a URL as the source.

candidates.label: evidenceOrigin
candidates.comment: An evidence origin relation between a medical guideline and the source of data used to formulate it. Also called: data source, guideline source, origin of evidence. Examples: "AHA Guideline for Hypertension" evidence origin "RCT", "NICE Guideline for Diabetes" evidence origin "Consensus Opinion", "WHO Guideline for COVID-19" evidence origin "Observational Studies". Distinct from evidenceLevel, which is the strength of the evidence.

candidates.label: claimInterpreter
candidates.comment: An interpretation relation between a claim and the organization or person who interpreted it from media content. Also called "interpreted by", "claim analyst", "fact-checker". Examples: "News claim claimInterpreter FactCheck.org", "Social media claim claimInterpreter Jane Doe".

candidates.label: studyLocation
candidates.comment: A geographic relation between a medical study and the administrative area where it is conducted or was conducted. Also called "research location", "trial site", "study area", "geographic scope of study". Examples: "The medical study has studyLocation New York", "The clinical trial's studyLocation is Europe", "This study is taking place in a specific studyLocation."

candidates.label: firstPerformance
candidates.comment: A first performance relation between a music composition and the event where it was initially performed. Also called: premiere, debut performance, initial staging. Examples: "Beethoven's 5th Symphony" first performance "Vienna, 1808 Concert", "Hamilton Musical" first performance "Public Theater, NYC 2015", "New Opera 'The Siren'" first performance "Royal Opera House Gala".

candidates.label: howPerformed
candidates.comment: A performance method relation between a medical procedure and a description of how it is carried out. Also called procedure steps, method of procedure, execution details. Examples: "A medical procedure has a description of how it is performed.", "The surgery details how it is performed.", "This procedure outlines how it is performed."

candidates.label: broadcastOfEvent
candidates.comment: An event that is being broadcast by a broadcast event. Also called: televised event, event broadcast. Examples: "BroadcastEvent 'Super Bowl Live' broadcastOfEvent 'Super Bowl LVIII'", "BroadcastEvent 'Concert Stream' broadcastOfEvent 'Live Music Concert'."

candidates.label: eventAttendanceMode
candidates.comment: An event attendance mode relation between an event and the enumeration indicating whether it occurs online, offline, or a mix. Also called "attendance format", "event delivery mode", "participation mode". Examples: "Event 'Conference' eventAttendanceMode 'OnlineEventAttendanceMode'", "Event 'Workshop' eventAttendanceMode 'OfflineEventAttendanceMode'", "Event 'Hybrid Meeting' eventAttendanceMode 'MixedEventAttendanceMode'".

candidates.label: studySubject
candidates.comment: An investigative relation between a medical study and the medical entity (condition, therapy, drug, etc.) that is being investigated. Also called "subject of investigation", "research focus", "entity studied", "trial subject". Examples: "The medical study has studySubject a new drug", "The clinical trial's studySubject is a specific medical condition", "This study investigates a studySubject therapy."

candidates.label: study
candidates.comment: A relation between a medical entity and a medical study or trial that investigates it. Also called "related study", "investigated by study", "medical trial". Examples: "The drug has study a clinical trial", "The medical condition is part of a study", "This therapy is being evaluated in a study."

candidates.label: isLiveBroadcast
candidates.comment: A broadcast status relation indicating whether a broadcast event is being transmitted in real-time. Also called live stream, real-time broadcast, live transmission. Examples: A sports game broadcast has isLiveBroadcast set to 'true'. A news report broadcast has isLiveBroadcast set to 'true'. A recorded TV show broadcast has isLiveBroadcast set to 'false'.

candidates.label: recordedIn
candidates.comment: A recording capture relation between an event and the creative work that captured all or part of it. Also called captured by, documented in, featured in. Examples: "A concert event was recorded in 'a live album'.", "A historical event was recorded in 'a documentary film'.", "A speech event was recorded in 'a news broadcast'.". Distinct from recordedAt, which is the inverse relation.

candidates.label: recordedAt
candidates.comment: A recording location relation between a creative work and the event where it was recorded. Also called recorded during, captured at event. Examples: "A live album was recorded at 'Wembley Stadium Concert'.", "A documentary film was recorded at 'the Amazon Rainforest Expedition'.", "A podcast episode was recorded at 'a conference panel discussion'.". Distinct from recordedIn, which is the inverse relation.

candidates.label: resultComment
candidates.comment: The specific comment created or sent as the outcome of a comment or reply action. Also called generated comment, comment outcome, produced comment. Examples: `CommentAction on Article` resultComment `User's Comment Text`, `ReplyAction to Forum Post` resultComment `Reply Comment`, `ReviewAction` resultComment `Reviewer's Feedback`. Distinct from `result`, which is a general outcome of any action.

candidates.label: rsvpResponse
candidates.comment: The specific response (e.g., Yes, No, Maybe) provided to an RSVP request. Also called RSVP status, attendance response, invitation reply. Examples: `Wedding RSVP` rsvpResponse `RsvpResponseType: Yes`, `Conference RSVP` rsvpResponse `RsvpResponseType: No`, `Party Invitation` rsvpResponse `RsvpResponseType: Maybe`.

candidates.label: interpretedAsClaim
candidates.comment: A claim extraction relation between a creative work or media object and a specific assertion or statement derived from its content. Also called contains claim, implies claim, claim extracted from, claim derived from. Examples: A news article is interpretedAsClaim 'The sky is blue'. A scientific paper is interpretedAsClaim 'Drug X cures Y'. A video is interpretedAsClaim 'Candidate Z made promise A'.

candidates.label: suggestedAnswer
candidates.comment: A proposed response or set of responses to a question. Also called "possible answer", "proposed solution", "answer option", "response to question". Examples: "The question has suggestedAnswer 'Yes'", "The quiz question's suggestedAnswer is a multiple-choice list", "This question provides a suggestedAnswer for users."

candidates.label: claimReviewed
candidates.comment: A summary relation for a claim review, providing a short text of the specific claims being reviewed. Also called "reviewed claim", "claim summary", "subject of review". Examples: "Fact-check review claimReviewed 'Eating apples cures cancer'", "Product claim review claimReviewed 'This product doubles battery life'".

candidates.label: error
candidates.comment: An error relation between a failed action and the thing providing more information on the cause of the failure. Also called "failure cause", "problem details", "issue description". Examples: "Action 'Payment' error 'Insufficient Funds'", "Action 'Login' error 'Invalid Credentials'", "Action 'File Upload' error 'File Too Large'". Distinct from errorCode, which is a specific code for the error.

candidates.label: question
candidates.comment: A question relation between an ask action and the specific question being posed. Also called asked question, inquiry. Examples: "An ask action involves the question 'What is the capital of France?'.", "A survey asks the question 'How satisfied are you with our service?'.", "A forum post poses the question 'How do I fix this error?'."

candidates.label: associatedClaimReview
candidates.comment: A claim review related to another review by common content, topic, or claim. Also called: related claim review, linked claim assessment. Examples: "Review 'MediaReview of Article' associatedClaimReview 'ClaimReview of Statement'", "Review 'FactCheck' associatedClaimReview 'Another FactCheck'". Distinct from associatedMediaReview, which links to a media review.

candidates.label: parentItem
candidates.comment: A hierarchical relation between a discussion item and its preceding item or a creative work it comments on. Also called part of, replies to, refers to, is a response to. Examples: A comment is a parent item of another comment. A question is a parent item of an answer. An answer is a parent item of a follow-up comment. Distinct from comment, which points from something to a comment about it.

candidates.label: claimInterpreter
candidates.comment: An interpretation relation between a claim and the organization or person who interpreted it from media content. Also called "interpreted by", "claim analyst", "fact-checker". Examples: "News claim claimInterpreter FactCheck.org", "Social media claim claimInterpreter Jane Doe".

relations.definition: To establish a collaborative relationship between two entities for a specific purpose.
relations.embedding_query_text: partnered_with: To establish a collaborative relationship between two entities for a specific purpose.

candidates.label: participant
candidates.comment: A collaborative relation between an action and an organization or person who indirectly participated in it. Also called collaborated with, involved, assisted by, co-agent. Examples: A writing action has a participant co-author. A research project has a participant researcher. A meeting has a participant attendee. Distinct from agent, which is the primary actor of an action.

candidates.label: bioChemInteraction
candidates.comment: A biochemical entity known to interact with another biochemical entity. Also called: biochemical interaction, molecular interaction, binding partner. Examples: "BioChemEntity 'Enzyme A' bioChemInteraction 'Substrate B'", "BioChemEntity 'Drug X' bioChemInteraction 'Protein Y'."

candidates.label: member
candidates.comment: A member relation between an organization or program membership and an organization or person belonging to it. Also called: belongs to, is a part of, participant in. Examples: "Club Organization member John Doe", "Team ProgramMembership member Jane Smith", "Alliance Organization member Partner Company". Distinct from memberOf, which expresses the inverse relationship.

candidates.label: knows
candidates.comment: A general acquaintance relation between two people who are known to each other socially or professionally. Also called acquainted with, familiar with, knows personally, has met. Examples: John knows 'Jane'. Sarah knows 'her colleague Tom'. The CEO knows 'the board members'. Distinct from follows, friend, or memberOf, which imply more specific types of relationships.

candidates.label: spouse
candidates.comment: A marital relation between two persons who are married to each other. Also called "husband", "wife", "married to", "partner". Examples: "John has spouse Jane", "Mary's spouse is David", "The couple includes a spouse relationship.". Distinct from colleague, which indicates a professional relationship, or parent, which indicates a familial relationship.

candidates.label: eligibleWithSupplier
candidates.comment: An eligible with supplier relation between a financial incentive and the organization that supplies the incentivized item or service. Also called "supplier partner", "incentive provider", "valid with retailer". Examples: "Rebate eligibleWithSupplier 'Utility Company X'", "Discount eligibleWithSupplier 'Electronics Store Y'", "Grant eligibleWithSupplier 'Solar Panel Installer Z'".

candidates.label: sponsor
candidates.comment: A support relation between an entity (creative work, event, grant, study, organization, or person) and the person or organization providing financial or other backing. Also called "funded by", "supported by", "patron", "underwritten by". Examples: "The event has sponsor Acme Corp", "The medical study's sponsor is the NIH", "This artist has sponsor a private foundation."

candidates.label: isRelatedTo
candidates.comment: A general association relation between two products or services that have some unspecified connection. Also called associated with, connected to, linked to, relevant to. Examples: A smartphone isRelatedTo 'a smart watch'. A car service isRelatedTo 'car insurance'. A book isRelatedTo 'a movie adaptation'. Distinct from isSimilarTo, which implies functional similarity, and isAccessoryOrSparePartFor or isConsumableFor, which imply specific functional dependencies. This is a very general relation.

candidates.label: about
candidates.comment: A subject matter relation between an entity (e.g., a creative work, event, or communication) and the topic it concerns. Also called concerning, regarding, on the topic of, related to. Examples: "A book about quantum physics.", "A lecture about climate change.", "A certification about data privacy."

candidates.label: colleagues
candidates.comment: A professional relation between a person and other persons who are their colleagues. Also called "co-workers", "associates", "professional peers". Examples: "John colleagues [Jane, Peter]", "Mary colleagues [Sarah, Tom]". Distinct from colleague, which is a singular form, though semantically similar.

candidates.label: manufacturer

candidates.label: mpn

candidates.label: productionDate

candidates.label: countryOfAssembly

Distinct from countryOfOrigin, which refers to the country of the principal offices or where the product originates.

candidates.label: costOrigin
candidates.comment: A source relation between a drug cost and additional details about where the cost data originated. Also called: cost data source, price origin, expense source. Examples: "Drug X cost" cost origin "Medicare Part B", "Medication Y price" cost origin "Private Insurance", "Prescription Z expense" cost origin "Manufacturer's List Price".

candidates.label: brand
candidates.comment: A brand or organization associated with a product, service, or maintained by an organization or person. Also called: product brand, service brand, corporate brand. Examples: "Product 'Smartphone' brand 'Apple'", "Service 'Cloud Storage' brand 'Google'", "Organization 'Company X' brand 'Brand Y'."

candidates.label: creator
candidates.comment: An authorship relation between a creative work or user comment and the person or organization responsible for its creation. Also called: author, originator, producer, made by. Examples: "Novel" creator "Jane Doe", "Software" creator "Acme Corp.", "Blog Post" creator "John Smith", "User Review" creator "Anonymous User". candidates.label: model
candidates.comment: A model relation between a product and its product model or textual identifier. Also called: product model, version, type. Examples: "Smartphone model 'iPhone 15 Pro'", "Car model 'Toyota Camry'", "Laptop model 'MacBook Air M2'".

candidates.label: countryOfOrigin
candidates.comment: A provenance relation between a creative work or product and its country of origin. Also called: origin country, produced in, made in. chosen_property.definition: A relation between an event and the overseas country it is directed towards.

candidates.label: returnPolicyCountry
candidates.comment: The country designated as the destination for product returns under a merchant return policy. Also called return destination country, country for returns, return shipping country. Examples: `US Return Policy` returnPolicyCountry `"US"`, `European Return Policy` returnPolicyCountry `Country: Germany`, `International Return Policy` returnPolicyCountry `"CA"`.

candidates.label: arrivalAirport
candidates.comment: An arrival airport relation between a flight and the airport where it concludes. Also called destination airport, landing airport, final airport. Examples: "A flight's arrival airport is 'LAX'.", "The flight's arrival airport is 'Heathrow Airport'."

candidates.label: itinerary
candidates.comment: A travel plan relation between a trip and the sequence of places or an item list detailing the destinations. Also called travel route, trip plan, destinations, journey path. Examples: A trip has an itinerary of 'Paris, Rome, London'. A trip has an itinerary of an ItemList detailing stops. A vacation package has an itinerary of 'Hawaii'.

candidates.label: departureAirport
candidates.comment: A geographical origin relation between a flight and the airport from which it originates. Also called: origin airport, departure airfield, flight departure point. Examples: "Flight BA249" departure airport "London Heathrow Airport", "Flight UA123" departure airport "San Francisco International Airport". Distinct from arrivalAirport, which is the destination airport.

candidates.label: toLocation
candidates.comment: A destination location relation between an action (like exercise, insert, move, or transfer) and the final place of the object or agent after the action. Also called destination, final location, arrival place. Examples: "MoveAction toLocation 'New York'", "TransferAction toLocation 'Warehouse B'", "ExerciseAction toLocation 'gym'". Distinct from location, which is the general place where something is or occurs.

candidates.label: arrivalTerminal
candidates.comment: A terminal identifier for a flight's arrival location. Also called: flight destination terminal, terminal of arrival. Examples: "Flight BA286 arrivalTerminal 'Terminal 5'", "Flight from Tokyo arrivalTerminal 'North Terminal'", "Flight to JFK arrivalTerminal 'Terminal 4'". Distinct from arrivalStation, which is for train trips.

candidates.label: departureStation
candidates.comment: A geographical origin relation between a train trip and the station from which it departs. Also called: origin train station, departure rail station, train departure point. Examples: "Train to Paris" departure station "London St Pancras International", "Commuter Train" departure station "Grand Central Terminal". Distinct from arrivalStation, which is the destination station.

candidates.label: shippingDestination
candidates.comment: The specified geographical region or regions where shipping is available or targeted. Also called delivery destination, shipping region, target delivery area. Examples: `Shipping Rate Settings` shippingDestination `DefinedRegion: US Postal Codes 90000-90210`, `Offer Shipping Details` shippingDestination `DefinedRegion: European Union`, `Delivery Time Settings` shippingDestination `DefinedRegion: North America`. Distinct from `shippingOrigin`, which is where the shipment comes from.

candidates.label: arrivalBoatTerminal
candidates.comment: An arrival boat terminal relation between a boat trip and the terminal or port where it concludes. Also called destination boat terminal, disembarkation port. Examples: "A boat trip's arrival boat terminal is 'Port of Miami'.", "The ferry trip's arrival boat terminal is 'Dover Terminal'."

candidates.label: deliveryAddress
candidates.comment: A destination relation between a parcel delivery and its destination postal address. Also called: shipping address, recipient address, delivery location. Examples: "Package" delivery address "123 Main St, Anytown, USA", "Food Order" delivery address "Apt 4B, 567 Oak Ave", "Mail" delivery address "P.O. Box 100".

chosen_property.label: geoCovers
chosen_property.justification: Reused schema.org 'geoCovers' in inverse direction for Country → Event.

candidates.label: speechToTextMarkup
candidates.comment: An identification of the markup format used for pronounceable text, such as SSML or IPA. Also called "pronunciation markup", "text-to-speech format", "phonetic notation". Examples: "The pronounceable text uses speechToTextMarkup SSML", "The dictionary entry has speechToTextMarkup IPA", "This text's speechToTextMarkup specifies pronunciation details."

candidates.label: startDate
candidates.comment: A temporal marker indicating the beginning date and time of an item, such as an event, program, or season. Also called "beginning date", "commencement date", "start time", "effective date". Examples: "The event has startDate 2023-10-26", "The program's startDate is September 1st", "This role's startDate was last Monday.". Distinct from dateCreated, which indicates when a creative work was first made.

candidates.label: geoCoveredBy
candidates.comment: A geo covered by relation representing a spatial relationship where a geometry or place is entirely covered by another geometry or place. Also called: is covered by, lies within, is contained by. Examples: "City 'Paris'" geo covered by "Country 'France'", "Lake 'Superior'" geo covered by "North America", "House '123 Main St'" geo covered by "City 'Springfield'". Distinct from geoCovers, which is the inverse relation.

candidates.label: tickerSymbol
candidates.comment: A textual identifier representing the exchange-traded instrument associated with a corporation, typically an exchange and instrument name. Also called "stock symbol", "stock ticker", "exchange symbol", "trading symbol". Examples: "Apple Inc. has tickerSymbol NASDAQ AAPL", "The corporation's tickerSymbol is NYSE GOOG", "This company is identified by its tickerSymbol."

candidates.label: startTime
candidates.comment: A temporal marker indicating the beginning time of an action, reservation, or media segment. Also called "beginning time", "commencement time", "start of action", "reservation time". Examples: "The reservation has startTime 7:00 PM", "The action's startTime was 10:30 AM", "The media clip's startTime is 00:01:15.". Distinct from startDate, which specifies a date, while startTime focuses on the time of day or an offset.

candidates.label: signDetected
candidates.comment: A medical sign or objective indicator identified through a medical test. Also called test finding, detected symptom, medical indicator. Examples: `Blood Test` signDetected `MedicalSign: Elevated White Blood Cell Count`, `X-Ray` signDetected `MedicalSign: Bone Fracture`, `Physical Exam` signDetected `MedicalSign: Swelling`. Distinct from `symptom`, which is a subjective experience.

candidates.label: birthDate
candidates.comment: A date representing a person's birth. Also called: date of birth, birthday. Examples: "Person 'John Doe' birthDate '1980-05-15'", "Person 'Jane Smith' birthDate '1992-11-22'."

candidates.label: identifier
candidates.comment: An identifier relation between any thing and a unique identifier for it. Also called ID, unique ID, reference number, code. Examples: "A product has an identifier 'GTIN123'.", "A person has an identifier 'UUID-XYZ'.", "This thing has an identifier URL."

candidates.label: isRelatedTo
candidates.comment: A general association relation between two products or services that have some unspecified connection. Also called associated with, connected to, linked to, relevant to. Examples: A smartphone isRelatedTo 'a smart watch'. A car service isRelatedTo 'car insurance'. A book isRelatedTo 'a movie adaptation'. Distinct from isSimilarTo, which implies functional similarity, and isAccessoryOrSparePartFor or isConsumableFor, which imply specific functional dependencies. This is a very general relation.

candidates.label: color
candidates.comment: A descriptive relation for a product, indicating its color. Also called "product color", "hue", "shade". Examples: "Car product color 'Red'", "Shirt product color 'Blue'". Distinct from colorSwatch, which provides an image of the color.
